name: Suriname
summary: A former Dutch colony, independent in 1975; one of the most ethnically mixed countries in the world, mostly covered by rainforest.

knownFor.label: Maroon communities
knownFor.note: Descendants of people who escaped slavery.

terrain.value: A narrow coastal plain of swamps and polders, a belt of savanna, and dense rainforest covering most of the interior uplands.

climate.value: Tropical and humid, with a long rainy season (about April–August) and a shorter one (about December–February).

resources.value: Gold, offshore and onshore oil, bauxite (mined from 1916 until 2017), timber and fish.

disasters.value: River and coastal flooding, such as the major interior floods of 2006, and erosion of the low-lying coast.

population.value: About 620,000 people (2024); the 2012 census counted about 541,000.

urbanisation.value: About half of all people live in Paramaribo, the capital, and its suburbs; the interior is very thinly settled.

disease.value: Malaria was once common in the interior but has been greatly reduced; dengue and Zika also occur.

migration.value: Many moved to the Netherlands around independence.

economicBase.value: Exports of gold, oil and (until 2017) alumina from bauxite, plus rice, bananas, fish and timber.

tradeRoutes.value: Seaborne trade through the port of Paramaribo; goods and gold move along rivers such as the Suriname and Marowijne.

wealth.value: An upper-middle-income country, but debt problems and high inflation in the early 2020s hurt living standards.

moneyAndTax.value: The Surinamese dollar, which replaced the Surinamese guilder in 2004.

inequality.value: Large gaps between the capital and rural areas.

governmentType.value: A parliamentary republic: the National Assembly elects the president, who is head of both state and government.

keyRulers.value: Johan Ferrier, first president (1975); Henck Arron, first prime minister; Dési Bouterse, who led a military regime after the 1980 coup.

succession.value: Under the 1987 constitution, the National Assembly elects the president after general elections held every five years.

institutions.value: The 51-seat National Assembly, the president and vice-president, the Council of State and the courts, under the 1987 constitution.

eliteConflict.value: Competition between political parties and leaders.

armyAndTech.value: The small Suriname National Army, which held power after the 1980 coup and fought the Interior War of 1986–92.

majorWars.value: The Interior War (1986–92) between the national army and the Maroon-led Jungle Commando, ended by a peace accord.

territoryChange.value: Border disputes with Guyana and French Guiana.

alliancesRivals.value: Close ties with the Netherlands, membership of the Caribbean Community (since 1995), and border disputes with Guyana and French Guiana.

inventions.value: No major inventions are associated with the modern state.

scienceEducation.value: The Anton de Kom University of Suriname (founded 1968) in Paramaribo; adult literacy is over 90%.

openness.value: Open to trade and foreign investment, with periods of restriction.

communicationTransport.value: Rivers and small planes link the interior; the East–West Link road runs along the coast, and the Jules Wijdenbosch Bridge crosses the Suriname River.

religion.value: Christians (about half), Hindus (about a fifth) and Muslims (about a seventh), plus Afro-Surinamese and Indigenous faiths.

languageWriting.value: Dutch is the official language; Sranan Tongo is widely spoken, alongside Sarnami Hindustani, Javanese, Maroon and Indigenous languages.

artsArchitecture.value: Wooden cathedral; mosque and synagogue side by side.

socialStructure.value: Indian, Creole, Javanese, Maroon, Indigenous and Chinese people.

sharedIdentity.value: Pride in many ethnic and religious groups living together, and the Sranan Tongo language, which most people share.

dailyLife.value: Many families eat roti, rice dishes, pom and Javanese bami; life centres on Paramaribo, while inland villages live along the rivers.

neighbours.value: Guyana to the west, French Guiana (France) to the east and Brazil to the south, with the Atlantic Ocean to the north.

ideasReligions.value: A tradition of religious tolerance: Paramaribo’s Neve Shalom synagogue stands beside a large mosque.

colonisation.value: Taken by the Dutch in 1667 (confirmed by the Treaty of Breda); plantation slavery lasted until 1863; independent in 1975.

riseSignals.value: Self-government within the Kingdom of the Netherlands from 1954, then full independence on 25 November 1975.

peakPeriod.value: Too recent to judge; the years after independence, with Dutch aid and bauxite income, are sometimes seen as prosperous.

declineSignals.value: None that define the country as a whole.

outcome.value: Still in existence as an independent republic with its capital at Paramaribo.

overallCertainty.value: Basic facts are well documented; some figures are estimates.
